packs.title: Arcades, Gardens and Open Views
packs.promise: Read open stonework, make small fictions and let three different outings change your view.

q.s: Collect an opening, a small shape and a solid wall.
st: From public space or the museum exterior photograph, find a broad lower arch, a small four-lobed opening in the upper arcade, and a patch of diamond-patterned wall above.
Draw or describe the three shapes as a vertical stack. Keep the differences between open space and solid stone visible.
Give your three-layer stack an original three-word title, with one word for each level.

q.s: Let a tree and an iron column exchange a thought.
st: From an open path, an available ordinary bench or the operator’s photograph, choose one tree feature and one iron pergola feature. Record both without touching or entering a bed.
Write an original four-line dialogue between those two features. Give the tree two lines and the iron two lines; let them disagree about the same small thing.
Add a one-sentence stage direction describing where their conversation takes place. Save the dialogue and stage direction.

q.s: Find a straight line, a curve and a repeated opening.
st: From public space or the restorer’s full facade photograph, find a straight horizontal tier, one upper curve and a repeated niche or window shape.
Draw or describe the three features separately, then connect them in a tiny facade diagram. Keep a blank gap for one opening.
Name your blank gap with one original word that describes how the surrounding shapes make it feel.

packs.title: Between Stone and Tide
packs.promise: Find a small story where Dorsoduro’s stone meets the water.

q.s: Make a tiny postcard from a triangle and a curve.
st: From a comfortable stopping place in the campo, find the large triangular outline at the top of San Barnaba’s façade and the curved top of its central doorway.
Use those two shapes to compose a tiny postcard: sketch them, or describe where they sit on your imaginary card.
Give the card an original three-word title. Add a one-sentence invitation inspired by the two shapes.
Save your two-shape card, title and invitation.

q.s: Collect the different textures of stone, water and sky.
st: Choose a comfortable place well back from the canal edge. Find three bands in your view: stone paving nearby, the Giudecca Canal beyond it and sky above.
Give each band one texture word based on what you see. Look for a second small detail in each band that supports your choice.
Order your three bands from the one that feels most still to the one that feels most changeable. There is no single correct order.
Save the three texture words, supporting details and your order.

q.s: Turn straight, curved and repeated details into a rhythm.
st: Look at a comfortable portion of the Gesuati façade from the public promenade.
Find a straight upright support, the curved feature above the main doorway and one detail that repeats on both sides.
Give your three finds a silent rhythm using short and long marks in your note. Repeat the pattern twice; change one mark in the second version.
Save the three architectural finds and both versions of the rhythm.
